questions.question: What is the primary non-renewable resource used to produce most traditional plastic food packaging?
options: Fossil fuels
Biomass
Geothermal energy
Solar radiation

questions.question: Why is traditional plastic waste in landfills and oceans considered a major pollutant?
options: It degrades extremely quickly and releases excessive heat
It takes a long time to degrade and can harm organisms
It dissolves instantly in water and causes extreme acidification
It acts as a fertilizer and causes runaway algal blooms

questions.question: What is a sustainable alternative to traditional plastic packaging that is made from renewable resources and breaks down naturally?
options: Polystyrene foam
Polyethylene wrappers
Biodegradable bioplastics
Synthetic nylon wraps

questions.question: What is a key benefit of using plastic packaging for food items?
options: It prevents food spoilage and reduces food waste
It permanently removes the need for refrigeration
It increases the vitamin content of the food
It makes the food completely calorie-free

questions.question: When deciding whether to use plastic packaging, what must we weigh its benefits against?
options: The taste of the food and consumer preferences
Emissions from production and damage to biodiversity
The cost of transporting the food by electric vehicles
The availability of solar-powered refrigeration units

questions.question: What is one of the major causes of global deforestation?
options: Converting land for agricultural use
Building offshore wind farms
Natural volcanic eruptions
The natural migration of forest animals

questions.question: What is a direct consequence of deforestation for many animal and plant species?
options: Increased availability of nesting sites
Habitat loss
A sudden decrease in global temperature
An increase in species diversity

questions.question: Which of the following is a land-use mitigation strategy that helps combat biodiversity loss and climate change?
options: Converting wetlands into housing estates
Reforestation and rewilding
Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers
Clearing forests for livestock grazing

questions.question: How does climate change make food production more challenging?
options: By decreasing the overall carbon footprint of farm vehicles
By making extreme weather events more common
By permanently removing all insect pests from crops
By increasing the amount of land available for farming

questions.question: How can individuals adjust their diet to help limit climate change?
options: By eating only foods imported from far away
By choosing food options that reduce emissions from production
By consuming more foods with high carbon footprints
By eating only foods packaged in non-recyclable plastic

questions.question: Why does deforestation disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: Fewer trees are available to release carbon dioxide into the soil
Less carbon dioxide is absorbed from the atmosphere for photosynthesis
It causes trees to absorb excessive amounts of oxygen
It stops animals from breathing out carbon dioxide

questions.question: What role does carbon dioxide (CO2) play in climate change?
options: It destroys the ozone layer directly to let in cosmic rays
It is a greenhouse gas that enhances the greenhouse effect
It cools the atmosphere by reflecting all incoming sunlight
It prevents clouds from forming in the upper atmosphere

questions.question: How does deforestation disrupt the water cycle?
options: Less water is absorbed and transpired by trees
It increases the overall level of atmospheric humidity globally
It prevents rain from falling anywhere on the planet
It forces plants to produce water through photosynthesis

questions.question: Why does the increased surface runoff caused by deforestation put food security at risk?
options: It increases flooding, which can damage crops
It causes all agricultural soils to turn into deserts instantly
It prevents rivers from flowing into the oceans
It reduces the amount of carbon dioxide available to crops

questions.question: Why might species be less well adapted to live in their current habitats due to climate change?
options: Climate change is changing the conditions in their habitats
Climate change is preventing species from reproducing at all
Species are choosing to lose their beneficial adaptations
Habitats are becoming completely isolated from the atmosphere

questions.question: How do some, but not all, species survive changes in environmental conditions caused by climate change?
options: By migrating to a new habitat
By instantly mutating to eat plastic waste
By entering permanent hibernation
By stopping their need for water and food

questions.question: What can be a direct result of climate change, including more frequent extreme weather events, on ecosystems?
options: An increase in the total number of new species created
Biodiversity loss
The complete elimination of the greenhouse effect
A reduction in agricultural land requirements
